title: Kotlin Language Traps: copy() Bypassing Validation
platform_conditions: Kotlin/JVM language semantics (data classes, smart casts, runCatching, when-exhaustiveness); applies to JVM and Android targets alike
security_mechanism: Data classes generate a public copy() that constructs a new instance without running the primary constructor's require()/init checks, so invariants enforced at construction ('role must be USER unless promoted') evaporate on the first copy(role = "admin"). Smart casts on shared var properties re-read the field after the check, so another thread's write between 'if (x is Admin)' and the use invalidates the cast's premise. runCatching { }.getOrNull() and '?: default' convert any authorization failure — including deliberate denial exceptions — into a silent null that downstream code may treat as 'unprivileged but valid', and a non-exhaustive when over a sealed hierarchy compiles to a fall-through that leaves unexpected roles at the else branch's (often permissive) behavior.

source_sink_clues.source: Request-derived user/role objects, deserialized models, and concurrent request threads mutating shared state used by authorization checks.
source_sink_clues.sink: user.copy(role = ...) on objects carrying authorization state; smart casts on shared mutable properties guarding security decisions; runCatching{}.getOrNull() / '?:' defaults around authentication or permission calls; non-exhaustive when on role/state enums

tracking_guards: Check privileged state transitions go through explicit validated functions rather than generated copy(); check security-relevant types are immutable vals (or custom classes without copy) whose init blocks validate; check auth failures propagate as thrown/returned denials instead of being collapsed by runCatching/elvis; check when blocks are exhaustive over the sealed hierarchy or end in a denying else.
not_candidate_when: copy() is used on DTOs with no authorization invariants and the privileged transition is gated server-side, the smart cast targets a local immutable value or the property is confined to one thread, or the when covers all cases with a default that denies rather than grants.
public_references: Kotlin documentation: null safety and smart casts — https://kotlinlang.org/docs/null-safety.html
